title: Machine learning prediction of CKD progression in hyperglycemic elderly adults: a prospective community cohort study

sections.title: 研究问题
sections.text:
《Machine learning prediction of CKD progression in hyperglycemic elderly adults: a prospective community cohort study》：研究问题的原文依据。

【Background · S0001-p3】Although multiple CKD prediction models exist for hyperglycemic individuals, most lack external validation, community application evidence and inclusion of prediabetic patients [14–18]. Machine learning (ML), a branch of artificial intelligence (AI), performs better than traditional statistical methods in predictive accuracy and enables scalable risk stratification using routine electronic health records (EHR) [19–20]. The American Society of Nephrology further points out that AI is widely applied in EHR documentation generation, and innovative AI based tools can provide actionable guidance for individual patients and nephrology specialists [21]. This prospective study aims to develop and externally validate an interpretable ML based CKD prediction model for community dwelling elderly hyperglycemic patients, covering both diabetic and prediabetic individuals. Ultimately, we aim to build a model that acts as a learning health system node to support better CKD management.

【Background · S0001-p1】Chronic kidney disease (CKD) represents a pressing global health crisis, impacting approximately 10% of the population worldwide [1]. By 2021, over 670 million people worldwide lived with CKD [2]. Projections to become the fifth leading cause of death by 2040, it underscores an urgent need for enhanced preventive strategies [3]. Hyperglycemia, spanning both prediabetes and diabetes, significantly elevates CKD risk through mechanisms like advanced glycation end-product accumulation, glomerular hyperfiltration, and microvascular damage [4]. Prediabetes is increasingly recognized as a substantial risk factor for CKD onset [5,6], while an estimated 40%–50% of individuals with diabetes will develop CKD [7,8]. Early screening for CKD risk in individuals with hyperglycemia is therefore critical for effective prevention and management.

sections.title: 研究方法
sections.text:
《Machine learning prediction of CKD progression in hyperglycemic elderly adults: a prospective community cohort study》：方法与研究设计的原文依据。

【Study design and participants · S0002-S2001-p1】This multicenter prospective cohort study adhered to TRIPOD-AI (Transparent Reporting of a Multivariable Prediction Model for Individual Prognosis or Diagnosis, Extended for Artificial Intelligence) and PROBAST-AI (Prediction model Risk Of Bias ASsessment Tool, Extended for Artificial Intelligence) guidelines to ensure transparent model development, validation, and bias assessment [22,23]. Completed TRIPOD-AI and PROBAST-AI checklists are provided in Appendix 1 and Appendix 2. The Medical Ethics Committee of Tongji University School of Medicine granted approval for this study (Ethics No. 2020tjdx068).

【Study design and participants · S0002-S2001-p2】We enrolled community-dwelling adults aged ≥60 years with hyperglycemia (including prediabetes and diabetes) from four Shanghai communities (Anting, Gonghexin Road, Huamu Road, and Nanxiang), all wih ≥ year annual follow-up. Study periods and sample sizes were as follows: Anting (2021–2024, n = 5862), Gonghexin Road (2016–2019, n = 3174), Huamu Road (2016–2018, n = 1981), and Nanxiang (2018–2021, n = 4561). Baseline data from Anting, Gonghexin Road, and Huamu Road were pooled and randomly split into training (80%, n = 8814) and internal test (20%, n = 2203) sets. Participants from Nanxiang served as the validation set. Participants were excluded in they had: (1) less than two follow-up visits; (2) age < 60 years; (3) normal glucose metabolism; (4) preexisting CKD; and (5) malignant tumors (Figure 1).

sections.title: 主要结果
sections.text:
《Machine learning prediction of CKD progression in hyperglycemic elderly adults: a prospective community cohort study》：结果的原文依据；数值与适用人群以引文为准。

【Conclusions · S0005-p1】We developed an interpretable ML model using the XGBoost algorithm, demonstrating robust predictive performance in internal and external validation. Packaged as an online application as a node of the learning health system, the tool enables efficient risk stratification, particularly critical for the high-risk subgroup (observed CKD incidence exceeds 50%), who require prioritized clinical intervention. Future research should incorporate more diverse, multi-dimensional datasets to strengthen the model’s representativeness and broader applicability.

【Figure 1. · F0001】Figure 1. The logic of data cleansing and analysis.

【Figure 2. · F0002】Figure 2. Boruta algorithm for variable selection in training data. (A) Feature importance ranking via the Boruta algorithm: The horizontal axis shows variable names, and the vertical axis represents Z-values for each variable. Box plots display Z-values calculated during modeling, with green boxes indicating important variables and red boxes indicating unimportant ones. (B) The iterative process of the Boruta algorithm.

【Figure 3. · F0003】Figure 3. Model evaluation in training set. (A) Calibration curves. The X-axis is the predicted probability, and the Y-axis is the actual occurrence probability, which are used to evaluate the model’s accuracy in predicting probabilities. (B) ROC curves. The X-axis represents the false positive rate (1 - specificity), and the Y-axis represents the true positive rate (sensitivity), which are used to evaluate the model’s discriminatory power. (C) Decision curves. The X-axis is the threshold probability, and the Y-axis is the net benefit, which are used to evaluate the model’s value in clinical decision-making.
